item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Z. None of the above

lookback_source.quote: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification, not how it is used, during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days

lookback_notes: The N0415 item box and coding instructions state a 7-day look-back/observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days). The N0415Z1 bullet itself refers to "the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)" without restating "7-day" (p. N-8). Counting convention (ARD + 6 previous calendar days) comes from the manual's general conventions (p. 2-17, p. 2-21), not from the item's own pages.

coding_levels.label: None of the above
coding_levels.definition: Check if none of the medications above (N0415A through N0415K) were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Condition not met
coding_levels.definition: Per the manual's general instructions for "check all that apply" items, the box is checked only if the specified condition is met; otherwise it remains blank. (General convention, not stated on the item's own pages.)

source.quote: Use a check mark for boxes where the instructions state to "check all that apply," if the specified condition is met; otherwise, these boxes should remain blank

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415Z1, None of the above, if none of the medications in classes N0415A–N0415K were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: N0415 is a "check all that apply" item; the None of the above row (Z) has only a Column 1 ("Is taking") check box and no Column 2 ("Indication noted") check box.

Column 1 of N0415 is checked if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days); high-risk drug class medications are coded according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: A medication is coded in N0415 even if it was given only once during the look-back period (therefore a single dose of any listed class precludes coding None of the above).

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly are counted only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication only if the patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root); over-the-counter sleeping medications are not coded as hypnotics.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Establishes the record basis for concluding that no listed high-risk class medication was received.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Outside-setting administrations must be ruled out before checking None of the above.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0 (e.g., manufacturer's package insert, resident's pharmacist).

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish to") with an expectation that sources are identifiable.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415Z to any payment or case-mix classification.
